summary: Build insurer-ready cyber risk assessments, control evidence, and board reporting in 5 days. Enquire now for TrainingCred.
lede: A cyber insurance readiness assessment helps security, risk and insurance professionals evaluate exposure and document evidence insurers may review. Participants map assets and controls, quantify potential losses using FAIR concepts, identify gaps in identity, backup, monitoring and incident-response evidence, and prepare risk registers, underwriting summaries and board briefings to support insurance decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to assess cyber insurance readiness, evidence control maturity, and support defensible insurance decisions. Cyber Risk Analyst responsible for quantifying exposure and prioritizing remediation. Information Security Manager overseeing control maturity and insurer-facing evidence. Cyber Insurance Broker preparing client submissions and coverage negotiations. Risk Manager aligning cyber exposure with enterprise risk appetite. Compliance Manager mapping security controls to policy and assurance needs. IT Governance Analyst maintaining cyber control inventories and action trackers. Incident Response Lead documenting readiness for claims and notification timelines. Internal Auditor testing evidence quality and control consistency. Third-Party Risk Specialist reviewing vendor exposure that affects coverage. Chief Risk Officer briefing leadership on cyber insurance readiness and residual risk.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of cybersecurity fundamentals, risk assessment concepts, and common security controls such as MFA, patching, logging, backup, and incident response. Familiarity with policy documentation, internal audit language, or insurance submission processes is helpful, but no programming is required. This course is positioned at an intermediate level, so you should already be comfortable reading security reports, interpreting control findings, and discussing risk with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
